name: --custom-property (CSS variable)
description: Declares a reusable custom value that can be referenced anywhere in the stylesheet via var(), and can be scoped or overridden per element.
notes: Unlike Sass variables, CSS custom properties are live in the DOM and can be read/changed with JavaScript or media queries.

name: var()
description: Reads the value of a CSS custom property, optionally falling back to a default if the property isn't defined.
parameters: --name — the custom property to read. fallback — optional value used if the property is unset.

name: calc()
description: Performs arithmetic (+, -, *, /) between mixed units directly inside a CSS value.
notes: Whitespace is required around + and - operators inside calc(), or the expression is invalid.

name: :root
description: Matches the document's root element (html), typically used as the conventional place to declare global custom properties.
notes: Behaves like the html selector but with higher specificity.

name: Specificity
description: The algorithm browsers use to decide which CSS rule wins when multiple rules target the same element, ranked roughly as inline styles > IDs > classes/attributes/pseudo-classes > element type selectors.
example: #nav .link { color: red; } /* wins over */ .link { color: blue; }
notes: !important and inline styles override normal specificity rules entirely, which is why overusing them makes CSS hard to maintain.

name: Cascade
description: The process by which browsers combine multiple CSS sources — origin (browser/author/user), specificity, and source order — to determine the final value of each property.
notes: When specificity is equal, the rule declared later in the source order wins.

name: Inheritance
description: Certain CSS properties, mostly text-related ones like color and font-family, are automatically passed down from a parent element to its children unless explicitly overridden.
notes: Layout properties like margin, padding, and border do not inherit by default; the inherit keyword can force any property to inherit explicitly.

name: Box model
description: The model describing how an element's total rendered size is composed of its content, padding, border, and margin layers.
notes: By default (content-box), width/height apply only to the content area — box-sizing: border-box makes them include padding and border instead.

name: CSS units (absolute vs relative)
description: CSS supports absolute units like px, which are fixed regardless of context, and relative units like %, em, rem, vw, and vh, which scale based on another value such as the parent, root, or viewport.
notes: Relative units are generally preferred for responsive, accessible layouts since they scale with user font-size preferences and viewport changes.

name: !important
description: Forces a declaration to override any other declaration for the same property, regardless of normal specificity rules.
notes: Generally considered a last resort — overusing it makes styles hard to override and debug later.

name: CSS reset / normalize
description: A base stylesheet applied first that removes or normalizes inconsistent default browser styling (margins, list bullets, font sizing) so components render predictably across browsers.

name: Shorthand properties
description: Properties like margin, background, font, and border that let you set several related longhand properties in a single declaration.
notes: Omitted values in a shorthand reset to their initial value, which can accidentally undo an earlier longhand declaration.

name: currentColor
description: A keyword that resolves to the element's own computed color value, useful for keeping borders, shadows, or fills in sync with text color.

name: Comments (/* */)
description: Marks text as a comment that is ignored by the browser, used to document or temporarily disable CSS rules.
notes: CSS has no single-line // comment syntax — only the /* */ block form.
